Sources & data notes

Source: NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD, historically ISH) station history, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/noaa/isd-history.csv (copy supplied to the build, not downloaded by this script), retrieved 14 September 2026. Basemap tiles are fetched live from OpenStreetMap and Esri; choose No basemap if you are offline. ISD is superseded. NCEI announced that it would not be updated beyond 2025-08-24 and that direct NCEI-hosted download would be retired on 2026-07-31, with NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD) as the continuing access path. The file used for this build does not match the announced date exactly: 8,985 records end on 2025-08-24, but 2,194 more run past it, to a maximum of 2025-08-28. Treat 2025-08-24 as the freeze and the few days beyond it as residual. Either way, a record ending at the freeze was active then, not necessarily active today. The colour coding is a derived classification by which identifiers a record carries (USAF, WBAN, both, neither); ISD publishes no network code. Records excluded for carrying no usable coordinate: 1,187 with a blank or unreadable latitude or longitude, and 379 more at exactly 0.000, 0.000, which is an ISD placeholder rather than a position in the Gulf of Guinea. Records reporting an elevation above 6,000 m: 4. These are plotted as published; several are the station number written into the elevation field and should not be trusted. BEGIN and END bracket the period of record and say nothing about gaps inside it: use isd-inventory.csv for station-year-month completeness before committing to a station for AERMET. Non-U.S. ISD data are subject to WMO Resolution 40 redistribution restrictions. This map is filtered to country code(s) US and is not the full global inventory. Download button: each station's popup can fetch and download that station's own most recent 5 years of raw ISD data directly from NCEI's per-station-year archive, concatenated into one multi-member gzip file (the format supports this; standard tools decompress the whole sequence as one continuous stream) — unlike the rest of this tool, that button needs a live internet connection at click time, and checks which of the last 10 calendar years actually exist for that station before fetching. NCEI has announced this direct-download path is slated for retirement in favor of NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD); if it disappears, this button will start failing even though the map itself keeps working.
